subject: Post-call: dedicated capacity sizing + $/1M token bands (Voltlytics)
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Chen <aaron@voltlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — dedicated capacity sizing + budget bands

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can build a tailored pilot quote. High-level from our notes:

- Stated monthly baseline: ~1.2B tokens/month (you mentioned seasonality ~+30% in Nov/Dec).
- Typical request payload: ~200–350 tokens; P95 target latency: <300ms for short chat flows.
- Peak concurrency window: morning business hours, ~100–150 concurrent users hitting the same route.

Open items for us to confirm so we can lock GPU SKU + reserved lanes and an expected $/1M token target:
1) Can you confirm the conservative monthly baseline you want Redwood to size for (baseline vs target peak month)?
2) What budget band are you comfortable with for unit economics (ballpark $/1M tokens)? You mentioned aiming for something between $600–$900/1M in the call — can you confirm a firm target or max?
3) Any hard constraints on GPU family? (e.g., must be A100 for procurement reasons, or open to H100/L40s).
4) Are you interested in a small reserved pilot (1 reserved lane for 30–60 days with burst capacity) or a larger 3–6 month reserved commitment?

What I’ll do next once you confirm 1–3: share a short pricing matrix (GPU options vs $/1M bands) and a pilot quote that shows expected tokens/day throughput per reserved lane and fallback options to hosted. Attached: a quick mapping doc and a draft pricing matrix (pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx).

Next steps (from our side):
- I’ll prepare a 30-day pilot proposal for 1 reserved lane + 50% burst buffer by Tue, 7 Dec.
- Ben will attach expected latency and tokens/sec estimates for H100 vs A100.

Thanks — happy to hop on 15 mins if you want to walk these numbers.

—
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com | (415) 555-0184

Attachments referenced: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), voltlytics-mapping-reqs.pdf (PDF of call notes)

From: Aaron Chen <aaron@voltlytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Morales <dana@voltlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 10:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — dedicated capacity sizing + budget bands

Monica — thanks for the clear note. Quick answers below: 

1) Baseline: let's size for 900M tokens/month conservative, but target ability to handle up to 1.5B in peak months.
2) Budget band: our procurement team is aiming at ~$650/1M tokens as the internal stretch. Max we can justify without exec approval is ~$800/1M.
3) GPU constraints: procurement prefers A100-series given existing vendor relationships, but we are open to H100 if the delta in unit economics is significant. 
4) Pilot: yes to a smaller pilot first — 30–60 day reserved lane with burst is preferred so we can validate latency and reliability.

Couple of follow-ups for your team:
- Can you show a simple table with: GPU SKU / expected tokens per month per reserved lane / estimated $/1M token at our band ($650 and $800)?
- What is the minimum monthly financial commitment for a single reserved lane pilot?
- Does Redwood support a brief (30d) trial that converts to a reserved commit with pro-rated credit if we convert?

If you can send the table and a recommended pilot configuration, we can route to procurement and legal.

Thanks — Aaron
Aaron Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Voltlytics
aaron@voltlytics.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Chen <aaron@voltlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 11:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — dedicated capacity sizing + budget bands

Aaron — great, thanks. Attached is the updated pricing matrix (pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx) and a one-page pilot recommendation. Quick answers inline and below: 

- Short table (high level):
  • H100 lane (1 reserved lane): ~400–500M tokens/month capacity at p95 latency target; indicative $/1M: $590 at your $650 band (volume discount applies as commit increases).
  • A100-80GB lane (1 reserved lane): ~300–380M tokens/month capacity; indicative $/1M: $740 at $650 band (A100 is slightly less efficient for your mix).
  • L40s lane (cost-optimized): ~250–320M tokens/month; indicative $/1M: $420 (but higher tail latency; recommended only for batch/async paths).

Notes on how we derived those: throughput is driven by model variant, sequence length profile, and KV-cache hit rate. The spreadsheet includes a small worksheet where we applied your median request length (250 tokens) and a conservative KV hit of 20% to estimate tokens/month per lane.

- Minimum financial commitment for a pilot lane: $15k/month reserved (this is our standard 1-lane 30–60d pilot price; final price is pro-rated if you convert to multi-month reserved).
- Trial conversion: yes — we can run a 30d pilot that converts to a reserved commit. If you elect to convert within the pilot window, we apply pro-rated credit for the portion of the pilot toward the committed term.

Recommended pilot (conservative):
1) 1x H100 reserved lane for 45 days (covers baseline + modest burst)
2) Autoscale burst to hosted pool up to 2x baseline during peak windows (no additional reserved cost but billed at hosted rates beyond burst allotment)
3) Success criteria: p95 latency <350ms, no more than 2% error rate, and cost per 1M tokens below $700 for the pilot month.

Next steps from us:
- I’ll send a formal pilot quote (with PO/contract language) and the pricing_workbook as a PDF for procurement.
- Ben will include an appendix with expected p95 latency numbers at 512-token requests for both H100 and A100.

Can you confirm internal approval for the $15k/month pilot and whether H100 is acceptable? If yes, I’ll attach an SOW and DocuSign link.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com | (415) 555-0184

Attachments referenced: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (updated), pilot_onepager.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Chen <aaron@voltlytics.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — dedicated capacity sizing + budget bands

Aaron / Monica — quick technical addendum from infra: 

- H100 vs A100: for your mix (250 median tokens, high KV reuse), H100 gives ~20–30% better token throughput and lower cost-per-1M at equivalent latency. That’s why H100 lane looks ~590/1M in Monica’s sheet vs ~740/1M for A100.
- Pilot sizing sanity check: 1x H100 lane at our conservative profiles should cover ~400M tokens/month with headroom for the 900M baseline if you route lower-latency routes to reserved and batch jobs to hosted. If Voltlytics needs to guarantee 1.2B baseline with no hosted spillover, we should plan for 3 lanes or a formal reserved commit that scales.
- Ops note: recommend we include a canary rollout + automatic fallback to hosted in the SOW and a 20% burst buffer for the pilot so we don’t throttle during ramp.

If procurement needs a short appendix on latency numbers (p50/p95/p99 at 256/512 tokens), we can drop that into the quote. Happy to join a call with procurement/legal if helpful.

—
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0110
